description:
Question. Query timing wraps execute plus full result receipt (base/sql_execution.py and each adapter's execute_query). Arrow-capable drivers could skip Python row building. Decide the contract for what a measured query interval contains and how results timed under the old contract stay distinguishable.

Facts. TPC-H 3.0.1 clause 5.3.7.2: a query interval ends at the last output character received by the driver (or at submission of the next query), so for TPC-H and TPC-DS metrics receiving the full result is inside the interval. Row building into Python tuples is a client representation choice, not required by the spec. Digest and validation already accept a lazy row source (compute_result_digest in base/sql_execution.py; MaterializedRowsSource and apply_materialized_result_validation in base/result_capture.py), so an Arrow result needs only a lazy Arrow-to-rows converter built outside the timer.

Options.
A. Full receipt inside the timer for all benchmarks; the driver may hand back rows or Arrow; record fetch_mode (rows|arrow) in result metadata; comparison refuses or warns across fetch modes. Recommended: keeps non-TPC results consistent with TPC results and is spec-consistent.
B. Exclude fetch for non-TPC benchmarks only. Inconsistent with TPC results; two contracts to maintain.
C. Exclude fetch for all benchmarks. Contradicts 5.3.7.2 for TPC metrics.

Evidence to prepare (agent, read-only): re-read 5.3.7.2 and the TPC-DS 4.0.0 query-interval clause and cite both; measure fetchall versus Arrow receipt of a large result on DuckDB (throwaway script) and record numbers; identify where fetch_mode would live in the result schema and whether result-schema-2-4-producer-20261022 is the right carrier; list adapters that cannot report rows_returned and so fall back to len(cursor.fetchall()).

Decision gate. Only the owner decides; the agent prepares the brief and then updates dependents.

Guardrails: read-only until the decision is recorded; no code, docs or priority changes except the dependents listed in the third acceptance criterion.
